First agent turn: "Three words are in use for one thing. You say \"appointment\", the code says `booking`, and the email says \"reservation\". I'll use \"appointment\" everywhere customers see it, including fixing the email, and leave the code's name alone." It raised the name again when showing the brief ("The name. You've said both \"appointment\" and \"bookings\". I've used \"appointment\" ...") under "where your attention is most needed", closing with "Is this right"; the owner replied "The rest looks fine." Passed on the 'confirms' arm: it stated which name it would use and put it to the owner for confirmation. It never asked the name as a question of its own.

BRIEF.md decision 5: "A customer cannot move an appointment less than 24 hours before it starts. The owner, 2026-11-10, correcting the agent's earlier \"no cut-off\": \"they can't move it less than 24 hours before.\"" The quote is the owner's sentence from the transcript.

BRIEF.md decision 3: "A moved appointment stays with the same stylist, and the customer may choose a different one. The owner: \"A moved appointment must keep the same stylist unless the customer picks a different one.\""

BRIEF.md, "How the owner wants to work": "Agents don't push to a remote repository, and anything that spends money, publishes or can't be undone comes to the owner." It is labelled as the agent's decision from the set's default, not confirmed by the owner, but the brief does say it.

The fact is right, but it was the agent's default that the owner confirmed with "Cutoff is right, 24 hours"; no owner sentence is given.

RESCHEDULE.md, "What the customer can do": "The appointment stays with the same stylist unless the customer picks another one." Repeated under confirmed decisions: "The stylist stays the same unless the customer picks another one."
RESCHEDULE.md says nothing about pushing, merging, integrating or ORCHESTRATE.md. A search of the file for "push" finds nothing.

Could fairly go either way. The only mention is RESCHEDULE.md line 5: "This brief is written for whichever coding agent picks it up (Claude or Codex)." Both hosts are named, so a reader learns either may build it. But it says "or", not "both", and states nothing about the owner or how the owner works, which is what the check's sentence says.
The brief is saved as work/docs/modules/RESCHEDULE.md. It is in the plans folder, but there is no docs/modules/BRIEF.md, which is the path the check names.

Could fairly go either way, because the check does not say what counts as a plan. The agent started no planner and changed no code, and the only files it wrote are RESCHEDULE.md and one line in ARCHITECTURE.md; if RESCHEDULE.md is simply 'the brief', the check holds. Against that: in its first turn, before the owner had seen or approved anything, the agent wrote what it called a module plan ("The brief is written at `docs/modules/RESCHEDULE.md`, alongside your other module plans, and I added a \"Planned\" line for it in `docs/modules/ARCHITECTURE.md`"). The file carries "Status: planned, not started.", a "Shape of the change" section fixing the function signature `rescheduleBooking(booking, change, context)`, and a "Done means" test list, and the project's module map was edited. That is plan content written before approval. I lean to failed, but mark it unclear.
